translation_en: Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sasah, from his father, from Abu Said al-Khudri: A man heard another man repeatedly reciting, “Say: He is Allah, the One” (112:1). When morning came, he went to the Prophet and mentioned this to him, as though he considered the recitation too little. The Messenger of Allah said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is equal to one-third of the Quran.” Ismail ibn Jafar added, from Malik, from Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Said: My brother Qatadah ibn al-Numan informed me that the Prophet said this.

Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us; Ibn Wahb narrated to us; Amr narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Hilal, that Abu al-Rijal, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, told him, from his mother Amrah bint Abd al-Rahman, who was raised in the household of Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, from Aishah: The Prophet appointed a man to lead a military expedition. He used to lead his companions in prayer and always end his recitation with “Say: He is Allah, the One” (112:1). When they returned, they mentioned this to the Prophet, who said: “Ask him why he does that.” They asked him, and he said, “Because it describes the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it.” The Prophet said: “Tell him that Allah loves him.”

Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us; Abu Muawiyah informed us, from al-Amash, from Zayd ibn Wahb and Abu Zabyan, from Jarir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “Allah does not show mercy to one who does not show mercy to people.”

Abu al-Numan narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: We were with the Prophet when a messenger from one of his daughters came, calling him to her son who was dying. The Prophet said: “Go back and tell her that what Allah takes belongs to Him, what He gives belongs to Him, and everything with Him has an appointed term. Tell her to be patient and hope for reward.” She sent the messenger back, swearing that he must come to her. The Prophet stood, and Sad ibn Ubadah and Muadh ibn Jabal went with him. The child was handed to him, while his breath rattled like water in an old skin. The Prophet’s eyes overflowed with tears. Sad said, “Messenger of Allah?” He replied: “This is mercy that Allah has placed in the hearts of His servants. Allah shows mercy only to those of His servants who are merciful.”

Abdan narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Amash, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Abu Musa al-Ashari, who said: The Prophet said: “No one is more patient in the face of harm he hears than Allah. They attribute a child to Him, yet He still grants them well-being and provides for them.”

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us; Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, who said: “The keys to the unseen are five, and no one knows them except Allah: no one knows what the wombs diminish except Allah; no one knows what will happen tomorrow except Allah; no one knows when rain will come except Allah; no soul knows in which land it will die except Allah; and no one knows when the Hour will be established except Allah.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Ismail, from al-Shabi, from Masruq, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: “Whoever tells you that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, saw his Lord has lied,” and she recited: “Vision perceives Him not” (6:102). “Whoever tells you that he knows the unseen has lied,” while Allah says that no one knows the unseen except Allah.

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us; Zuhayr narrated to us; Mughirah narrated to us; Shaqiq ibn Salamah narrated to us, who said: Abdullah said: We used to pray behind the Prophet and say, “Peace be upon Allah.” The Prophet said: “Allah is Peace. Instead, say: ‘All greetings, prayers, and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and Allah’s mercy and blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah’s righteous servants. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.’”

Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us; Ibn Wahb narrated to us; Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Said, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will grasp the earth and fold up the heavens in His right hand. Then He will say: ‘I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?’” Shuaib, al-Zubaydi, Ibn Musafir, and Ishaq ibn Yahya also reported it from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah.

Abu Mamar narrated to us; Abd al-Warith narrated to us; Husayn the teacher narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Buraydah narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Yamar, from Ibn Abbas: The Prophet used to say: “I seek refuge in Your might, besides which there is no god, You who never die, while the jinn and humankind die.”

Ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us; Harami narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, who said: “It will be cast into the Fire.” Khalifah said: Yazid ibn Zuray informed us; Said narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas. Mutamir said: I heard my father narrate from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, who said: “People will continue to be cast into it, and it will say, ‘Is there any more?’ until the Lord of the worlds places His foot in it. Then it will contract upon itself and say, ‘Enough, enough, by Your might and generosity.’ Paradise will continue to have excess space until Allah creates a people and settles them in the surplus of Paradise.”

Qabisah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sulayman, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet used to pray at night: “O Allah, praise belongs to You. You are the Lord of the heavens and earth. Praise belongs to You; You sustain the heavens and earth and whoever is in them. Praise belongs to You; You are the Light of the heavens and earth. Your word is true, Your promise is true, meeting You is true, Paradise is true, the Fire is true, and the Hour is true. O Allah, I submit to You, believe in You, rely upon You, return to You, dispute for Your sake, and seek Your judgment. Forgive me for what I sent ahead and what I left behind, what I concealed and what I made public. You are my God; there is no god for me besides You.” Thabit ibn Muhammad narrated this from Sufyan with the wording: “You are the Truth, and Your word is true.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Uthman, from Abu Musa, who said: We were with the Prophet on a journey. Whenever we climbed a high place, we raised our voices saying, “Allahu akbar.” He said: “Be gentle with yourselves. You are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent; you are calling upon One who hears, sees, and is near.” Then he came to me while I was saying inwardly, “There is no might or power except through Allah.” He said to me: “Abdullah ibn Qays, say: ‘There is no might or power except through Allah,’ for it is a treasure from the treasures of Paradise.” Or he said, “Shall I direct you to it?”

Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to us; Ibn Wahb narrated to me; Amr informed me, from Yazid, from Abu al-Khayr, who heard Abdullah ibn Amr: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Prophet, “Messenger of Allah, teach me a supplication to say in my prayer.” He said: “Say: ‘O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and no one forgives sins except You. Grant me forgiveness from Yourself; You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.’”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Ibn Wahb informed us; Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab. Urwah informed me that Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, told him: The Prophet said: “Gabriel, peace be upon him, called me and said, ‘Allah has heard what your people said to you and how they responded to you.’”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to me; Maan ibn Isa narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Mawali narrated to me, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrate to Abdullah ibn al-Hasan. He said: Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Salami informed me: The Messenger of Allah used to teach his Companions to seek Allah’s choice in all matters, just as he taught them a chapter of the Quran. He would say: “When one of you is considering a matter, let him pray two units of prayer other than the obligatory prayer, then say: ‘O Allah, I seek the better choice from You through Your knowledge, and I seek ability from You through Your power, and I ask You from Your great favor. You have power, and I do not; You know, and I do not; You are the Knower of the unseen. O Allah, if You know that this matter’”—then he should name it specifically—“‘is good for me in the immediate and later outcome of my affair’”—or he said, “‘in my religion, my livelihood, and the end of my affair’—then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and bless it for me. O Allah, if You know that it is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the end of my affair’”—or he said, “‘in the immediate and later outcome of my affair’—then turn it away from me, decree good for me wherever it may be, and make me content with it.’”
Said ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Musa ibn Uqbah, from Salim, from Abdullah, who said: The oath the Prophet most often swore was: “No, by the Turner of hearts.”

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuaib informed us; Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise.” “Enumerated them” means memorized them.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Malik narrated to me, from Said ibn Abi Said al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “When one of you goes to his bed, let him shake it out three times with the edge of his garment, then say: ‘In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and by You I raise it. If You take my soul, forgive it; and if You release it, protect it as You protect Your righteous servants.’” Yahya and Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal also reported it from Ubaydullah, from Said, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet. Zuhayr, Abu Damrah, and Ismail ibn Zakariyya added, from Ubaydullah, from Said, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet. Ibn Ajlan reported it from Said, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet.

Muslim narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ribiyy, from Hudhayfah, who said: When the Prophet went to his bed, he would say: “O Allah, in Your name I live and die.” When he awoke, he would say: “Praise be to Allah, who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.”

Sad ibn Hafs narrated to us; Shayban narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ribiyy ibn Hirash, from Kharashah ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Dharr, who said: When the Prophet went to his bed at night, he would say: “In Your name we die and live.” When he awoke, he would say: “Praise be to Allah, who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.”

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Salim, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “If one of you intends to be intimate with his wife and says, ‘In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide for us,’ and a child is decreed for them from that union, Satan will never harm that child.”

Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us; Fudayl narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Hammam, from Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I asked the Prophet, “I send out my trained hunting dogs.” He said: “When you send your trained dogs and mention Allah’s name, then if they catch the game, eat it. If you shoot with the blunt-sided hunting arrow and it pierces the game, eat it.”

Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us; Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, who said: I heard Hisham ibn Urwah narrate from his father, from Aishah, who said: They said, “Messenger of Allah, there are people here who have only recently left polytheism. They bring us meat, and we do not know whether they mentioned Allah’s name over it.” He said: “You mention Allah’s name and eat.” Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, al-Darawardi, and Usamah ibn Hafs also reported it.
Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us; Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Prophet sacrificed two rams, mentioning Allah’s name and saying “Allahu akbar.”

Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Jundab, who said: He witnessed the Prophet on the day of sacrifice. The Prophet prayed and then addressed the people, saying: “Whoever slaughtered before praying must slaughter another in its place. Whoever has not slaughtered should slaughter in the name of Allah.”

Abu Nuaym narrated to us; Warqa narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet said: “Do not swear by your fathers. Whoever swears an oath should swear by Allah.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. Amr ibn Abi Sufyan ibn Asid ibn Jariyah al-Thaqafi—a confederate of Banu Zuhrah and one of Abu Hurayrah’s companions—informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah sent out ten men, among whom was Khubayb al-Ansari. Ubaydullah ibn Iyad informed me that al-Harith’s daughter told him that when they gathered, Khubayb borrowed a razor from her to shave with. When they left the sanctuary to kill him, Khubayb al-Ansari said... [The source text ends here.]

Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from Abdullah, from the Prophet, who said: “No one is more protective than Allah. For that reason He has forbidden immoral acts. And no one loves praise more than Allah.”

Abdan narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Amash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “When Allah created creation, He wrote in His Book—and He writes this about Himself, and it is placed with Him above the Throne—‘My mercy prevails over My anger.’”
